card.summary: The newest LTX flagship (2.5, 22B) — distilled, text→video, the ComfyUI int8-convrot build on 24 GB. New Gemma-4-12B text connector; single-stage path. The text→video counterpart to the LTX-2.5 image→video editor.
card.pick_when: You want the newest LTX (2.5) text→video on a 24 GB card.

prompt.guidance: Describe the scene, motion, and camera; the prompt directs everything.
prompt.example: a fox trots across a snowy clearing at dawn, the camera tracking alongside, soft morning light, cinematic
prompt.overview: For LTX-2.5 text-to-video, write a single present-tense paragraph that establishes the subject and setting, then directs the motion, camera, and (for audio-capable endpoints) sound — the model invents everything from the text.
prompt.instructions: Because there is no source frame, name the subject and setting up front, then spend most of the prompt on motion: how subjects move, how the camera behaves, and how the scene evolves. LTX-2.5's Gemma-4-12B text connector is highly responsive to fine detail, so a longer, granular single paragraph (chronological action beats, explicit camera moves, lighting, ambient sound) reliably outperforms a short one — and short prompts on long clips make the model rush. Lead with one main action, layer precise chronological detail, put camera and lighting last, and match prompt length to clip length (~one main action per 2-3 seconds). Write present tense.
do: Name the subject and setting first, then build motion and camera on top
Write a single flowing paragraph in present tense, in chronological order
Name camera moves explicitly - 'slow dolly in', 'tracking shot', 'jib up', 'static locked-off'
Express emotion through physical cues (weight shift, head turn, widening eyes), not abstract labels
Match prompt length and detail to clip length; ~one main action per 2-3 seconds
Describe audio (ambient, voice quality, dialogue in quotes) for audio-capable endpoints
Specify lighting concretely and describe how the scene looks after a camera move
dont: Don't omit the subject/scene - text→video invents everything from the words
Don't overload with many subjects or 4-5 distinct actions - the model compresses or skips them
Don't use vague/metaphorical language or numerical micro-specs ('pan 2 degrees/sec')
Don't give conflicting directions ('running quickly in slow motion', 'still lake with crashing waves')
Don't rely on readable on-screen text/logos or chaotic complex physics
examples: A lone lighthouse stands on a rocky headland at dusk, its beam sweeping slowly through thickening fog. The camera begins wide and low, then pushes in gradually as waves break harder against the rocks and the beam passes across the lens. The light shifts from deep blue to the warm pulse of the lamp; distant surf and a low foghorn fill the soundtrack.

A slow dolly-in pushes toward a mountain peak as low clouds drift from left to right across the ridgeline. The light shifts gradually from dawn orange to clean midday white, mist creeps up the slope, and the foreground pines sway gently before the camera settles into a steady wide hold, ambient wind rising.
prompt.negative_guidance: A negative prompt is optional but a short one (e.g. 'blurry, distorted, extra limbs, warped face, flickering, watermark, text') can nudge the result closer to intent.
